name: Blocks (Mission Control)
description: The interactive Mission Control map with objects an AeroVLA-OFT sentence can name. The map is Project AirSim Blocks as shipped, with its own blue cone and orange ball; the pads, the cubes and the cylinder are the shared catalogue's objects (configs/targets/objects.json), added at run time on open ground. No terrain, building or wall is added or moved; the one structure of this file is a flat plate on the orange ball, and it exists only in the layout `mission_cap`. Blocks is one of the scenes the model was trained in; this arrangement of objects is new. Read by src/visual_search/maps.load_map like the maps under configs/maps/, and kept outside that folder because it belongs to a demonstration, not to an evaluation.

structures.name: OrangeBallCap
structures.note: A flat round plate on the map's own orange ball, in the layout `mission_cap` only. The ball is 10 m across and its top is 9.7 m above the ground; 3 m from its axis its surface lies 1.0 m below the top, so a plate of 3 m radius standing from 8.7 m to 9.9 m rests on the ball all round and has a flat top 0.2 m above it. Not an obstacle of its own: it stands inside the ball's footprint.

landing_caps.description: Objects given a flat top they do not have by themselves (configs/landing/surfaces.json, `cap`): layout -> object -> the structure that is the plate. Only in `mission_cap`; in `mission` the orange ball is a sphere and nothing can land on it.

mission.description: What the interactive mission adds to the map. `launches` are poses on open ground: the canonical evaluation measures every height from where the vehicle rests at the start, and the map's own spawn point is a platform 1.5 m above the ground, from which a touchdown on a 2.5 m pad would be read as a collision. A launch also stands more than 16 m from the nearest block: nearer, a turning vehicle faces a wall that fills its view, and the policy answers that by climbing (seen in the first trial of this map, 8.5 m from a block). Every mission starts from the selected launch the way an evaluation episode starts. `instructions` name the sentence templates of configs/visual_search.json; the words themselves are not repeated here.

launches.name: North field
launches.note: Both pads in the first view, each with the cube of its own colour on its outer side; the green cylinder behind.

launches.name: South plaza
launches.note: The map's own blue cone straight ahead, between the grey blocks.

start.description: A start placed by the user (S on the map, or -StartX / -StartY / -StartYaw / -StartHeight of the launcher) instead of a preset launch. It is flown exactly as a preset is: the scene is loaded with the vehicle at that place and heading, and it climbs to that height (src/mission/start.py). The rule a start has to meet takes every number from where it already exists and none is written here: clearance from every obstacle and object as a planned evaluation start keeps it (configs/visual_search.json, generalization.start_margin_m), a height between the executor's floor (configs/flight_limits.json, minimum_clearance_m) and the map's ceiling (altitude.ceiling_m above), on open ground inside the map's area. A preset or a start without a height starts at the evaluation's cruise height (configs/visual_search.json, cruise_height_m). The two steps below are how far one key press moves the height and the heading.
